subject: Architecture
title: The Twin Towers: Radical Engineering
description: A 60-second lesson on The Twin Towers: Radical Engineering.

hook.text: The World Trade Center's Twin Towers used a structural system no skyscraper had ever tried before.

buildup.text: Engineer Fazlur Khan proposed a tube structure — closely spaced exterior columns carrying all the load.

discovery.text: The tube system eliminated interior columns, creating massive open floor plates ideal for offices.

twist.text: Critics initially hated the plain design. Architecture magazines called the towers boring boxes.

climax.text: At 1,368 feet each, the towers briefly held the world's tallest record before the Sears Tower surpassed them.

punchline.text: They weren't loved for beauty. They were loved for being there.

quiz.question: What innovative structural system did the Twin Towers use?
options: A central concrete core with cantilevered floors
A tube of closely spaced exterior columns carrying the load
Cross-braced steel trusses visible from outside

details.summary: The World Trade Center Twin Towers, completed in 1973, used a revolutionary tube-frame structure — a dense grid of exterior columns carried wind loads while the core handled gravity loads. At 417 meters, they were briefly the world's tallest and redefined structural engineering for supertalls.
details.whyItMatters: The tube-frame concept eliminated interior columns, creating vast open floor plates. This structural innovation influenced every supertall building that followed and remains fundamental to skyscraper engineering today.
takeaways: Completed in 1973 using innovative tube-frame structure
Exterior columns carried wind loads; core handled gravity
The design created column-free open floor plates

faq.question: What made the Twin Towers' structure innovative?
faq.answer: Engineer Fazlur Khan's tube concept placed closely spaced steel columns around the perimeter, creating a rigid hollow tube that resisted wind forces. The central core handled vertical gravity loads. This separation of functions allowed immense height with open, flexible floor plans.

faq.question: How tall were the Twin Towers?
faq.answer: The North Tower reached 417 meters and the South Tower 415 meters. They were the world's tallest buildings from 1973 until the Willis Tower surpassed them in 1974. Both towers were destroyed in the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.
